Nielsen Norman Group
UX research guideline for dashboard data visualization.
Explain how to design at-a-glance dashboards that communicate critical quantitative information quickly using preattentive visual attributes.
Single-screen at-a-glance dashboard layouts contrast operational monitors with analytical summaries; examples include bar and line charts, scatterplots, bullet charts versus gauges, and cautions against pie, donut, and 3D charts.
Linear article reading with static example dashboards used as evidence rather than an interactive product flow.
Responsive editorial web article; examples are static screenshots rather than a live authenticated product surface.
Enterprise analytics and operational-monitoring screenshots such as ArcGIS emergency dispatch and sales trend dashboards.
Grounds chart choice in preattentive processing and quantitative readability
Separates operational real-time monitoring from analytical review use cases
Provides concrete do-and-don't comparisons such as bullet charts over gauges
Product-agnostic theory with limited guidance on card composition or navigation
Examples skew toward BI dashboards rather than creator-home layouts
Does not address personalization or notification prioritization
Prefer length and 2D position encodings for KPI tiles and charts
Design operational homes for immediate action and analytical homes for slower review
Avoid angle- and area-heavy chart types on dense creator dashboards
